Locke leads the office responsible for the certification, production approval, and continued airworthiness of aircraft; and certification of pilots, mechanics, and others in safety-related positions. Previously, Locke was Executive Director for Aircraft Certification Service (AIR), overseeing type certification, production approval, airworthiness certification, and continued airworthiness of the U.S. civil aircraft fleet, including both commercial and general aviation . Before that, Locke served as Director of AIR’s Compliance & Airworthiness Division, where she managed a broad portfolio of certification and validation projects. Earlier in her FAA career, Locke served as acting deputy executive director and chief of staff of Flight Standards. She also served as Deputy Executive Director of the Office of Rulemaking, and as a Senior Technical Advisor in AVS. Locke joined the FAA in 2008. The Bureau of Land Management (BLM) has completed the sale of approximately 2.97 acres of federal land at the Calcasieu Pass Radio Beacon Station in Cameron Parish, Louisiana. The sale returns an isolated federal parcel to productive use and supports development of adjacent energy infrastructure. The parcel was originally reserved in 1875 for lighthouse operations and later managed by the U.S. Coast Guard. On July 3, 2025, the Coast Guard formally notified the BLM that it no longer had an operational need for the property and intended to relinquish custody, accountability, and control of the land. By default, these calendars have Monday as the first day of the week, and Sunday as the last (the European convention). Use setfirstweekday() to set the first day of the week to Sunday (6) or to any other weekday. Parameters that specify dates are given as integers. For related functionality, see also the datetime and time modules. The functions and classes defined in this module use an idealized calendar, the current Gregorian calendar extended indefinitely in both directions. This matches the definition of the “proleptic Gregorian” calendar in Dershowitz and Reingold’s book “Calendrical Calculations”, where it’s the base calendar for all computations. Zero and negative years are interpreted as prescribed by the ISO 8601 standard. Year 0 is 1 BC, year -1 is 2 BC, and so on. class calendar. DOE supports the development, standardization, and maintenance of calibration facilities for environmental radiation sensors. Radiation standards at the facilities are primarily used to calibrate portable surface gamma-ray survey meters and borehole logging instruments used for uranium and other mineral exploration and remedial action measurements. Standards for calibrating borehole fission neutron devices are also available, but are used infrequently. Radiation standards are constructed of concrete with elevated, uniform concentrations of naturally occurring potassium, uranium, and/or thorium. Pad standards have large, flat surfaces suitable for calibration measurements with portable surface survey meters. Borehole standards are large concrete cylinders with 4.5-inch-diameter test holes. In our everyday lives, calibrations are often the little adjustments you may make, for example to make sure the colors of your computer monitor or television are accurate, so it will show photos or videos the way that a filmmaker or photographer intended. But for a scientific measurement laboratory such as NIST, calibrations are a bit different. NIST calibrations determine a relationship between the measurement standard (like the Kibble balance) and that instrument or object (such as a cylindrical metal kilogram mass). By using a world-class reference such as the Kibble balance, calibrations make it possible for a piece of measuring equipment to make the most accurate measurement it can. By Nate Blakeslee Photographs by Aaron Huey Published November 3, 2026 Susan H ar t firs t no t iced the wolves one summer about six years back. They’d pop up in the evenings on the ridges of the ranch she runs with her husband, Blair, whose family has raised cattle near Montague, California, since 1852. The Harts are one of the oldest ranching families in Siskiyou County, an enormous, sparsely populated region of rugged mountains and pristine valleys near the Oregon border. The most frequent visitor Susan saw was a wolf with a distinctive light coat and an injured foreleg that spent a lot of time watching the herd. It was clearly too slow to catch a mule deer, the most common prey animal in the nearby mountains, and Susan was worried that it was just a matter of time before it became bold enough to attack one of her animals. pages.text: Call Protocol — Python 3.16.0a2 documentation Navigation index modules | next | previous | Python » 3.16.0a2 documentation » Python/C API reference manual » Abstract Objects Layer » Call Protocol | Theme Auto Light Dark | Call Protocol ¶ CPython supports two different calling protocols: tp_call and vectorcall. The tp_call Protocol ¶ Instances of classes that set tp_call are callable. The signature of the slot is: PyObject * tp_call ( PyObject * callable , PyObject * args , PyObject * kwargs ); A call is made using a tuple for the positional arguments and a dict for the keyword arguments, similarly to callable(*args, **kwargs) in Python code. args must be non-NULL (use an empty tuple if there are no arguments) but kwargs may be NULL if there are no keyword arguments. This convention is not only used by tp_call : tp_new and tp_init also pass arguments this way. To call an object, use PyObject_Call() or another call API . The Vectorcall Protocol ¶ Added in version 3.9. The vectorcall protocol was introduced in PEP 590 as an additional protocol for making calls more efficient. As rule of thumb, CPython will prefer the vectorcall for internal calls if the callable supports it. However, this is not a hard rule. Additionally, some third-party extensions use tp_call directly (rather than using PyObject_Call() ). Therefore, a class supporting vectorcall must also implement tp_call . Royaume-Uni) VUE D'ENSEMBLE DE L'AFFAIRE La République du Cameroun s’est plainte de ce que le Royaume-Uni avait violé l’accord de tutelle s’appliquant au territoire du Cameroun sous administration britannique (divisé en Cameroun septentrional et Cameroun méridional) du fait que la tutelle avait abouti au rattachement du Cameroun septentrional au Nigéria et non à la République du Cameroun, dont le territoire avait été auparavant administré par la France et auquel avait été rattaché le Cameroun méridional. Le Royaume-Uni a soulevé des exceptions préliminaires à la compétence de la Cour. La Cour a estimé qu’une décision judiciaire sur le fond du différend serait sans objet puisque, comme la République du Cameroun l’avait reconnu, un arrêt de la Cour ne pouvait avoir d’effet sur la décision de l’Assemblée générale stipulant le rattachement du Cameroun septentrional au Nigéria conformément aux résultats d’un plébiscite surveillé par les Nations Unies. En conséquence, par arrêt du 2 décembre 1963, la Cour a déclaré ne pouvoir statuer au fond sur la demande de la République du Cameroun. Cette vue d’ensemble de l’affaire est donnée uniquement à titre d’information et n’engage en aucune façon la Cour. Hide cookies message Skip to main content About Camp 144 at Kew This temporary installation displayed photographs from the prisoner of war camp that was located on the site of The National Archives in Kew in 1945. The land The National Archives stands on once housed a complex of buildings known as Camp 144. In July 1945, about 2,300 Italian prisoners of war were held in the camp. Italy had surrendered in 1943 and many Italian POWs were then categorised as ‘co-operators’ and put to work outside their camps and granted some freedoms. When not working they could travel up to 5 miles away, but weren’t allowed to visit shops, cinemas or pubs. If invited, they could visit local people in their homes. The ‘co-operators’ living at camp 144 worked on properties across London that had been damaged by V1 and V2 rockets. The war in Europe ended in May 1945 but many Italian POWs did not start being repatriated until December, as they were still needed for the work they were doing across the country. The site provides outdoor recreation opportunities in a non-motorized natural setting for 400,000 to 500,000 visitors annually. The 25-mile trail system winds through the woods, providing year-round recreation opportunities on unpaved trails that link to the adjacent 4,000 acre Far North Bicentennial Park trail network managed by the Municipality of Anchorage Parks and Recreation Division (MoA). Popular activities include walking, running, mountain biking, horseback riding, and wildlife viewing. In the winter, activities include snowshoeing, fat tire biking, skijoring, and cross-country skiing. Users can access Campbell Tract SRMA from the BLM’s Smokejumper Trailhead and Campbell Airstrip Trailhead and the MoA Abbott Loop Community Park Trailhead.
